name: EZIO8SA
description: An 8-output, 7-input Insteon/X10 controller with Form C relays. It connects to Insteon through a PowerLinc Modem plugged into its PLM port; its inputs are 4 opto-isolated, 2 analog and one 1-Wire input.

verification.note: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) assigns 0x07/0x04 to the Compacta EZIO8SA I/O Module; the EZIOxx Advanced Details give 0x07/0x02 for EZIO as a whole. The catalog uses 0x07/0x04, the model's own entry.
The EZIOxx Advanced Details cover the whole EZIOxx line, from inputs-only to outputs-only models, and warn that a model may not support every command.
The Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA links input N by tapping the SET button N times; that input N sends group N is read from that. The EZIOxx Advanced Details let each input's group number be changed.

The catalog numbers the groups as its linking steps count the outputs, so this group's responder record, and On and Off for it, reach output 8.

The Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA links output N by tapping the SET button N times; numbering the outputs as groups follows that. steps.text: Connect one end of a straight-through CAT5 patch cable to the RJ-45 connector on the bottom of the PLM.
Plug the other end of the patch cable into the PLM port on the EZIO8SA.
Plug the PLM directly into an AC outlet, away from low-voltage transformers, surge protectors and other devices that cause line noise.
Connect a 9 to 18 V DC adapter, center positive, to the EZIO8SA's 9-18VDC port.
Plug the adapter into an AC outlet.

notes: The EZIO8SA needs an Insteon PowerLinc Modem (PLM), dual-band recommended, which the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA says isn't included. The EZIO8SA & PLM Combo comes with the modem and a 12 V DC adapter.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button on the EZIO8SA's PLM for 10 to 12 seconds.
Release the SET button.
Tap the SET button once for input 1, twice for input 2, and so on.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 5 seconds.
Release the SET button.
Press the SET button on each device to be controlled.
Press and hold the SET button on the EZIO8SA's PLM for 3 to 5 seconds to finish linking.

notes: This links an input as a controller. The Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA and the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA & PLM Combo give the same steps, on the SET button of the PowerLinc Modem (PLM) connected to the EZIO8SA.
Linking mode lasts 4 minutes, for adding several responders, unless the last step ends it first.

X10: relays 1 to 8 answer units 1 to 8 of any house code. To enable X10, press and hold the SET button on the PLM for 3 to 5 seconds and release it (the status LED blinks), then send an X10 On 3 times, such as A1, A On, A1, A On, A1 On; the status LED stops blinking. An Off disables it. The Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA holds the SET button for 3 to 5 seconds, has the relays answer any house code and disables X10 with one Off; the EZIOxx Advanced Details choose the house code on the X10 controller first, hold the SET button for at least 4 seconds, and send 3 Off commands to disable X10. This note follows the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA.

steps.text: Put the controller in linking mode, usually by pressing and holding its SET button for 3 to 5 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button on the EZIO8SA's PLM for 3 to 5 seconds.
Release the SET button.
Tap the SET button once for output 1, twice for output 2, and so on.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 5 seconds.
Release the SET button.

notes: To link a snapshot of all the relays, set them to the positions wanted first, then skip the taps. The controller's command then puts every relay back in the position it had when linked.
A controller's button can be linked to only one output; a later link from it to an output replaces the earlier one.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button on the EZIO8SA's PLM for 3 to 5 seconds.
Release the SET button.
Tap the SET button once, for output 1.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 5 seconds.
Release the SET button.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, for output 1, and the device's group 1, input 1, to the Hub as a controller, so the Hub receives the input's reports. Link inputs 2 to 7 the same way, with cmd2 0x02 to 0x07.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub. The EZIOxx Advanced Details give Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with the group number in cmd2, but don't say whether it links an input as a controller, and neither the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA nor the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA & PLM Combo says how the EZIO8SA answers messages sent to its PLM.

steps.text: Unplug the PLM.
Wait at least 10 seconds.
Press the SET button while plugging the PLM back in.
Keep holding the SET button for 3 to 5 seconds, until the buzzer stops.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED goes out for a second and comes back on when the reset is done

notes: The Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA and the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA & PLM Combo give these steps, on the PLM connected to the EZIO8SA, as the EZIO8SA's factory reset; they don't say what it erases.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a controller and as a responder.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Repeat the last two steps for each other input linked to the Hub, groups 2 to 7, with cmd2 set to the group (0x02 to 0x07).
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub. The EZIOxx Advanced Details give Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) and Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with the group number in cmd2.

notes: Neither the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA nor the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA & PLM Combo gives a model number; the profile is named for the product.
Outputs 7 and 8 are swapped: to control output 8, address output 7, and the other way around.

As a responder, a record whose Data 2 is 0x01 triggers the input in Data 3 (0x00 for input 1) as if it had turned on, so the input sends its own group command. The EZIOxx Advanced Details allow it for inputs 1 to 7, but neither the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA nor the Quick Start Guide - EZIO8SA & PLM Combo gives a way to link one, and groups 1 to 7 are also outputs 1 to 7, whose responder records the catalog gives for those groups.
An EZIComm 5010K connected to the PLM port in place of the modem doesn't power the EZIO8SA, so the EZIO8SA still needs its own DC adapter.
Each relay is Form C (SPDT), rated 3 A at 24 V DC or 120 V AC, with CM, NC and NO terminals. Output timers run from 1 to 255 seconds or minutes.

Inputs 1 to 4 (DI1 to DI4) are opto-isolated and need 3 to 30 V DC; a dry contact can use the 12 V DC terminal. Inputs 5 and 6 (Anl1, Anl2) are digital by default, on at 0 to 1 V DC and off at 2 to 3 V DC, or analog for 0 to 3 V DC sensors with trip points from 0 to 1023; ground them if unused, or they send constant Insteon traffic. Input 7 is 1-Wire, for a DS18B20 temperature sensor.
An EZEye light sensor on an analog input reads 1023 counts at about 3 V.
